'''Annette Lykknes''' is a Norwegian chemist and historian, and is a full professor at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]]. She publishes on the history of chemistry, particularly the history of the periodic table, and women's roles in chemical discoveries. Lykknes is Chair of the Division of [[History of chemistry|History of Chemistry]] of the [[European Chemical Society]].

==Academic career==

Lykknes trained as a teacher and taught at high school.<ref name=":0" /> She completed an MSc in chemistry and chemistry education in 1998, followed by a [[PhD]] on Norwegian [[Radiochemistry|radiochemist]] [[Ellen Gleditsch]] at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lykknes |first=Annette |title=Ellen Gleditsch : professor, radiochemist, and mentor |date=2006 |access-date=20 June 2025 |type=PhD |publisher= |url=https://bibsys-primo.hosted.exlibrisgroup.com/permalink/f/1bcqu3e/BIBSYS_ILS71503654700002201}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Lykknes then joined the faculty of the university, where she is professor of chemistry education.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Women's History Month: Meet Annette Lykknes |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/page/pressroom/2020-03-10-01 |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=World Scientific Publishing |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hickman |first=Daniel |date=2019-09-03 |title=A Fresh View on the History of Science |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/11175112/A_Fresh_View_on_the_History_of_Science/ |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=ChemistryViews |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lykknes is Chair of the Division of History of Chemistry of the European Chemical Society, a position she has held since 2021, and was vice-chair from 2011. She is a delegate of the [[Norwegian Chemical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Division of History of Chemistry |url=https://www.euchems.eu/divisions/history-of-chemistry-2/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=EuChemS |language=en-US}}</ref> Lykknes is also a member of the Commission on the History of Women in Science, Technology, and Medicine of the [[International Union of History and Philosophy of Science|International Union for the History of Science, Technology and  Medicine]]. She is the topical editor for History of Chemistry for the Springer-published ''ChemTexts: The Textbook Journal of Chemistry''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ChemTexts |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/40828/updates/17317006 |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=SpringerLink |language=en}}</ref> She has contributed articles on the [[periodic table]] and [[Law of mass action|mass action law]] to the ''[[Great Norwegian Encyclopedia|Store Norske Leksikon]]'', and is subject manager for articles in the categories History of Chemistry, Chemists, and the Periodic Table.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annette Lykknes |url=https://brukere.snl.no/36643 |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=Bidragsytere |language=no |archive-date=23 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523053822/https://brukere.snl.no/36643 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2022, she was guest editor of a special issue of ''[[Ambix]]'', on women scientists, along with Elena Serrano and Joris Mercelis.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ambix, Volume 69, Issue 3 (2022) |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/toc/yamb20/69/3 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=Taylor & Francis |language=en |archive-date=8 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220808004158/https://www.tandfonline.com/toc/yamb20/69/3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

With [[Brigitte Van Tiggelen]], Lykknes co-edited the book ''Women in their Element: Selected Women's Contributions to the Periodic System'', which was published by World Scientific in 2019. The book includes biographies of thirty-eight women who contributed to the discovery of elements, with a particular focus on scientific collaborations.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dabkowska |first=Hanna A. |date=2020-10-01 |title=Women in their element – selected women’s contributions to the periodic system: edited by Annette Lykknes and Brigitte Van Tiggelen, 2019, World Scientific Publishing Co., Singapore, 556 pp., GPB 115 (hardcover, excluding postage), GBP 19.90 (e-book), ISBN 978-981-120-628-3 (hardcover), ISBN 978-981-120-630-6 (e-book) |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0889311X.2020.1825399 |journal=Crystallography Reviews |language=en |volume=26 |issue=4 |pages=272–273 |doi=10.1080/0889311X.2020.1825399 |issn=0889-311X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Carneiro |first=Ana |date=May 2021 |title=Edited by Annette Lykknes, Brigitte van Tiggelen. Women in their element: Selected women's contributions to the periodic system. Singapore, Singapore: World Scientific, 2019, xxiv + 531 pp. {{text|ISBN}}: 9789811206283 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1600-0498.12339 |journal=Centaurus |language=en |volume=63 |issue=2 |pages=431–433 |doi=10.1111/1600-0498.12339 |issn=0008-8994 |archive-date=8 December 2021 |access-date=21 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208115456/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1600-0498.12339 |url-status=live |hdl=10362/135412 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Lykknes also co-wrote ''Periodesystemet: Fra alkymi til kjernekjemi'' [''The Periodic Table From alchemy to nuclear chemistry''], commissioned by the Norwegian Cultural Council, which was shortlisted for the Norwegian University of Science and Technology Literature Award in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eikeseth og Lykknes: Periodesystemet |url=https://museumsforlaget.no/produkt/periodesystemet/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=Museumsforlaget |language=nb-NO |archive-date=12 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250512045443/https://museumsforlaget.no/produkt/periodesystemet/ |url-status=live }}</ref> A volume containing didactic materials about chemical histories titled ''Discovering the Elements: No Simple Stories'' and edited by Lykknes and Van Tiggelen is due to be published in November 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Discovering the Elements {{!}} Analysis: Historical Cases in Chemistry |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/14334 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.worldscientific.com |language=en |doi=10.1142/14334}}</ref>
